Looking at the cuboid (3×2×2), I can label positions (x: 1–3 left→right, y: 1–2 front→back, z: 1–2 bottom→top).

- **Grey piece (visible):** top front row (1,1,2), (2,1,2), (3,1,2) plus (1,1,1) — complete (4 cubes).
- **Dark piece (visible):** (2,1,1), (3,1,1), (3,2,1) — needs one hidden cube.
- **White piece (visible):** top back row (1,2,2), (2,2,2), (3,2,2) — needs one hidden cube.

The only hidden cubes are (1,2,1) and (2,2,1). The dark piece must take (2,2,1), otherwise its cube at (1,2,1) would be disconnected from the rest. So the white piece gets (1,2,1).

**White piece:** a straight row of three cubes with one cube attached below the end of the row — an L-shape (planar). Rotating this gives a column of three cubes with one cube sticking out at the top end, which is exactly diagram B.

\boxed{B}
